main_text.l: ILLVSTRISSIMO FLORENTISSIMOQVE PRINCIPI AC DOMINO, DOMINO FRIDERICO IV. Comiti Palatino ad Renum, Duci Bauariæ, Sacri Rom. Imperij Archidapifero & Electori, Domino ac Principi suo clementissimo:

l.i: ILLVSTRISSIME PRINCEPS ELECTOR, Domine clementissime, Multa requiruntur in bono Principe, Dei inter homines vicario: inter alia, singulare eius ornamentum & præsidium longè optimum est sapientia, quæ diuinarum & humanarum rerum cognitionem complectitur. Hinc Plato Resp. tum demum felices fore censebat, si aut Principes philosopharetur, aut Philosophi Respubl. administrarent. Et, ut tefte vtar graviore, sapientum multitudo est mundi salus, & rex prudens stabilimentum populi, inquit Sapiens. Quocirca etiam mortalium ille sapientissimus rex Salomon, filius Dauid, cum tenella ætate, regni gubernacula accepisset, oblata à Deo optione petendi quod à y vellet,

page.notes: Reading of the Greek-looking ornament band and some italic words is approximate; the marginal reference "Sap. 6." is at the right, beside the line "populi, inquit Sapiens." Several words in the italic opening are doubtful, notably "tefte" and "à y", which appear to be printed reference marks and a corrupt word.
